column11: CheckMate 9X8 (Lenz et al., J Immunother Cancer 2024;12(3):e008409, doi:10.1136/jitc-2023-008409, PMID 38485190; NCT03414983): median PFS by BICR of 11.9 months on mFOLFOX6 plus bevacizumab in first-line mCRC. The nivolumab arm had the same median (HR 0.81)
column12: Constant hazard from a median: 1 - 0.5^(12/11.9) = 0.503. This is the form the PF-08634404 and vepugratinib seeds use, not the brief's 1 - exp(-12/m), which treats the median as a mean. CheckMate 9X8's control arm is the same backbone as INCA033890-303's, and it is the only randomised trial of a PD-1 added to that backbone in this line. Case for higher: real-world first-line chemotherapy plus bevacizumab runs shorter. Bevacizumab-naive US patients had a median rwPFS of 8.6 months (Jin et al., Ther Adv Med Oncol 2023, doi:10.1177/17588359231182386), which gives 0.620. Immune add-ons also add toxicity stops: grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs were 75% vs 48% in CheckMate 9X8. Case for lower: a positive INCA33890 arm would by design extend PFS

Reused from the PF-08634404 seed, which covers the same first-line MSS pool. Three filters multiplied. (1) 35.1% metastatic: the telisotuzumab adizutecan seed's SEER derivation. (2) 55.9% receive chemotherapy: 47,026 of 84,161 US patients newly diagnosed with metastatic CRC, NCDB 2006-2011 (Krell et al., Cancer 2015, doi:10.1002/cncr.29253). (3) 88.6% both mismatch-repair proficient and BRAF wild-type: 2,713 of 3,063 first-line trial patients after removing 153 dMMR and 197 pMMR BRAF-mutant tumours (Venderbosch et al., Clin Cancer Res 2014, doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-14-0332). 0.351 x 0.559 x 0.886 = 0.1738, about 27,600 patients a year
column12: The filters match INCA033890-303's entry criteria. The trial takes stage IV disease not amenable to curative resection with no prior systemic therapy for metastatic disease, and excludes MSI-H/dMMR and BRAF V600E tumours (NCT07284849, as returned by search of the ClinicalTrials.gov record and site listings). Case for lower: the label will be with bevacizumab. RAS wild-type left-sided patients usually receive anti-EGFR therapy instead, and the trial also requires measurable disease and ECOG 0-1. None of these is filtered here, because I found no US share to source for them. The NCDB chemotherapy share dates from 2006-2011

column11: Two measured factors multiplied. (1) The reach of a bevacizumab backbone in this pool: bevacizumab, the first biologic added to first-line chemotherapy in metastatic colorectal cancer and the regimen INCA33890 is given with, was used by 57.6% of SEER-Medicare stage IV colon cancer patients starting first-line FOLFOX or FOLFIRI in 2013, down from 68.2% in 2005; 2,352 of 3,785 (62.1%) over 2005-2013 (Raab et al., Clin Colorectal Cancer 2019;18(3):e294-e299, doi:10.1016/j.clcc.2019.05.008, PMID 31266707). (2) The share of its backbone a PD-1 add-on took: nivolumab-containing regimens were 34.7% of first-line starts among 2,029 US Medicare fee-for-service patients with HER2-negative advanced gastric/GEJ cancer, 2021-2024 (Chen et al., J Manag Care Spec Pharm 2026;32(7):807-819, doi:10.18553/jmcp.2026.32.7.807, PMID 42341069). 0.347 x 0.576 = 0.1999
column12: Judgement on the second factor; the first is measured in this disease, line and payer. Nivolumab's gastric label rides on fluoropyrimidine-platinum chemotherapy, which almost every first-line patient already receives, so its 34.7% is a share of its backbone. INCA033890-303 adds to chemotherapy plus bevacizumab, and in Medicare only 57.6% of first-line doublet patients get bevacizumab, so the researcher's 0.347 applied to the whole eligible pool counted patients on chemotherapy alone or anti-EGFR regimens that the label's regimen does not reach. The PF-08634404 seed's 0.20 for this pool is not a measurable anchor: its source reads only 'a share of the pool above, set against what the molecule has to displace'. Bevacizumab is the only measured first-line entrant in MSS-dominated colorectal cancer; BRAFTOVI's first-line regimen (2024) is in BRAF V600E tumours, which this trial excludes, and no uptake share was found for it. Case for higher: bevacizumab took 62.1% of its own backbone in Medicare over 2005-2013, and using that as the add-on share gives 0.576 x 0.621 = 0.358, close to the researcher's figure; nivolumab's 34.7% averages 2021-2024 including the launch year, and the PD-1 class took 44.6% in Medicare; an effective add-on could move chemotherapy-alone patients onto bevacizumab, which is now biosimilar and cheap. Using the 2005-2013 average reach gives 0.347 x 0.621 = 0.215. In all-age US data bevacizumab was still 60% (965 of 1,607) of first-line left-sided RAS/RAF wild-type patients in 2013-2018, with anti-EGFR only 12% (Nevala-Plagemann et al., J Natl Compr Canc Netw 2022, doi:10.6004/jnccn.2021.7079, PMID 35120306). Case for lower: every PD-1 tried in MSS colorectal cancer has failed, CheckMate 9X8 included; this trial's primary endpoint is PFS, where nivolumab's gastric label rested on overall survival; Raab's cohort is colon only and FOLFOX/FOLFIRI only; anti-EGFR use in left-sided RAS wild-type disease has grown since 2013; a web search summary of the trial listings describes the backbone as FOLFOX with bevacizumab, and a label restricted to an oxaliplatin backbone would narrow the reach further; PF-08634404 competes for the same patients (the book's pool_crowding module scales both if their claims exceed the pool). About 5,500 US patients a year at peak (158,850 x 0.1738 x 0.1999).
